slides.title: From decisions to a working admin foundation.
slides.lead: ShelfLife progress report · October 4–17, 2026
slides.body:
6setup steps implemented
74local test cases passed
5connected UI groups passed

A detailed account of the requests, decisions, implementation and evidence that moved the project forward—including documented weekend work.
slides.caption: October 16 · Actual Flutter application connected to the disposable backend.

slides.title: The most meaningful change
slides.lead: The project moved beyond a sample cockpit into a locally implemented and partially connected admin setup flow.
slides.body:
Direction became explicit

Staff journeys, approval responsibilities, offline boundaries and paired rounds were documented and accepted.

Configuration became editable

Admins can define store details, product packs, locations, presets and action policies, then review a configuration version.

Claims gained runtime evidence

SQL, real sign-in, permission denials, concurrent writers, DTO parsing, restart persistence and baseline restoration were exercised.

As of the reporting cutoff: connected application validation was still in progress. This was not a production launch.

slides.title: Fourteen calendar days. Clear evidence boundaries.
slides.lead: Sunday October 4 through Saturday October 17, inclusive. Prepared October 19 from saved records.
slides.body:
Recorded activity

October 9–13 and 15–16 have dated checkpoints or event evidence. Saturday 10 and Sunday 11 contain substantial documented work.

Reconstructed interval

October 14 sits inside the approved October 13–15 implementation period. The report describes that interval without inventing exact daily completion timestamps.

No dated entry

October 4–8 and 17 have no specific execution entry in the reviewed packet. They remain visible in the daily log; absence of evidence does not prove inactivity.

Screenshots are real saved project captures. Fixture images, connected application captures and the older demo are labeled separately. No invented hours, releases or photo evidence.

slides.title: What was complete—and what was still open
slides.lead: These are different levels of completion, not one blended percentage.
slides.body:
Accepted

Design & scope

Workflow decisions, six-step onboarding and bounded S1 acceptance plan.

Implemented

Admin foundation

Flutter screens, typed client, draft states, versioned SQL and permission checks.

Verified locally

Backend & recovery

Runtime checks and corrected baseline restore on a synthetic disposable target.

In progress

Full app acceptance

Five UI groups passed; activation, recovery, identity and lifecycle checks remained.

The next verified milestone is October 9: the project adopted chapter closeouts, a session index, a stable handoff pointer and explicit approval boundaries.

slides.title: A repeatable chapter workflow
slides.lead: The project gained a reliable way to preserve decisions and resume work.
slides.body:
• DocumentedStanding chapter instructions, implementation plan, status ledger, session index and a stable next-handoff pointer.
  • PreservedOriginal chats remained the audit record for exact approvals, inputs and outputs. New dated handoffs supplemented them.
  • TransitionedOne fresh Staff Workflow Design Specification chat was created with an explicit in-chat start gate.
Scope on this day: workflow documentation. No new application implementation, deployment or connected testing.

slides.title: The major design decisions landed
slides.lead: Weekend work defined how people, approvals and configuration should fit together.
slides.body:
• Specification13 screens, six workflow areas, 28 proposed acceptance scenarios and ten source gaps were documented.
  • Human decisionsLead/admin confirmations, offline limits, lock timing, catalog review and paired rounds were accepted.
  • Product directionCustomizable admin presets and first-use setup replaced the need to hardcode every store’s policy. The combined design was accepted.

slides.title: Evidence was reconciled and the design chapter closed
slides.lead: The team corrected an earlier premature verification claim and completed the written-design checkpoint.
slides.body:
• VerifiedThe resumed closeout checked 49 protected files, 26 preserved ledger events and 56 local references.
  • CorrectedA prior credit-related interruption was explicitly recorded instead of presenting an unexecuted verification as complete.
  • Handed offOne fresh scope-and-acceptance chapter was created, with design acceptance carried forward and implementation still separately gated.

slides.title: Admin Setup became the first implementation slice
slides.lead: The broad staff vision was narrowed into a bounded first deliverable.
slides.body:
• Defined S1Admin identity, saved/resumable six-step setup, versioned presets, prerequisites and explicit configuration activation.
  • Mapped acceptanceTwelve S1 scenarios, AC01–AC34 coverage across later slices, file boundaries, persistence/API proposals and action approvals.
  • Showed existing workThe existing sample demo loaded; inventory lookup and checklist progress were observed. This was not a new release.

slides.title: A tangible demo, more data and implementation approval
slides.lead: Requests connected the design discussion to visible, testable work.
slides.body:
• DemonstratedThe sample preview saved Whole milk, 2 units, with an October 15 expiry. The displayed activity was session-only.
  • ExpandedA local CSV and preview catalog grew to 20 fictional, unique, checksum-valid UPCs; legacy aliases and derived totals were retained.
  • ApprovedAdmin Setup Foundation and R02 installed-dependency local checks were authorized. The initial preview baseline passed 3/3 tests.

slides.title: Implementation and review interval
slides.lead: Reconstructed placement within the documented October 13–15 source-work window.
slides.body:
Source work in the interval

Typed setup models and validation, controller/repository behavior, six-step UI, admin gate and matching SQL/assertion source.

Review work in the interval

Readiness handling, active-version consistency, visible discard/reload, preset descriptions and session/dialog protection were addressed.

Dating limit

The October 15 closeout establishes completion and results. It does not independently prove which edit or test occurred specifically on October 14.

RECONSTRUCTED INTERVAL · No hours, exact sequence or per-day completion is claimed. A timestamp inside a widget fixture is sample data, not proof of its capture date.

slides.title: Local implementation reached its checkpoint
slides.lead: The admin foundation passed local checks; the next chapter began isolated backend verification.
slides.body:
• Local result73 combined tests plus one accessibility test passed; whole-app offline analysis was clean. Desktop and 390px widget captures were saved.
  • Backend scopeR03/R06 approved a pinned CLI and isolated synthetic backend. Seven migrations applied and SQL assertions passed.
  • Runtime evidenceConcurrency, real Auth/API and restart tests passed. Unexpected wildcard bindings were stopped and corrected before acceptance testing.
The initial Docker failure and initial wildcard exposure interval were retained as limitations. No production deployment or publication was made.

slides.title: Recovery succeeded and real UI testing began
slides.lead: A corrected restore completed; the actual Flutter app reached the disposable backend.
slides.body:
• Strengthened checksA fresh 19-group concurrency run passed; 61 captured responses decoded through production Dart models.
  • RecoveredAn initial restore failed with the limited postgres role. After explicit approval, the existing supabase_admin role restored the baseline; migrations and assertions passed again.
  • Validated UIThe web build succeeded. Five Chrome groups passed for real sign-in, drafts, packs, locations and presets. All six setup pages were inspected.

slides.title: The period-end position
slides.lead: No new execution entry was found for October 17; this slide carries forward the last evidenced state.
slides.body:
Ready to continue

The admin foundation, backend validation evidence and successful restore were available. Actual connected Chrome checks had started.

Still to finish

UI activation, two-session conflicts, uncertain-response retry, offline recovery, identity changes, lifecycle locking and narrow authenticated layouts.

Still separate

Production hosting, publication, merging, rollout, physical-device tests and later staff workflows were not completed by this reporting cutoff.

CARRY-FORWARD SNAPSHOT · This is not a claim of Saturday execution. October 19 events are outside the requested reporting period.

slides.title: “Continue the chapter cycle.”
slides.lead: Keep work bounded and make every chapter easy to audit.
slides.body:
• What you asked forFinish verification, update the plan/status, save an executive summary and engineering handoff, and index the exact source chat.
  • What changedThe project adopted preserved dated records, explicit chapter ownership and a stable pointer to the latest handoff.
  • Why it mattersA new chat carries a concise handoff without replacing the original record. Transition permission remains distinct from permission to begin work.

slides.title: “Customizable presets … on the admin’s discretion”
slides.lead: Your request made onboarding the place to collect real store rules.
slides.body:
“then on onboarding, prompt them their first initial set up.”

Response

A six-step store setup and editable preset design was accepted, then implemented as the S1 foundation.

Impact

Jurisdiction, units, packs, labels, locations and handling policies are supplied explicitly instead of invented as universal defaults.

Boundary

Unknown prerequisites keep affected capabilities unavailable. Saving a draft does not silently activate it.

slides.title: Show the existing work
slides.lead: The demonstration request established what was already real and what was still only specified.
slides.body:
Observed

The hosted sample cockpit loaded; inventory lookup, checklist progress and a sample batch-save flow were shown.

Captured

An October 13 screenshot records one batch tried and the Whole milk activity with 2 units.

Clarified

This was the older sample preview with session-only state—not the new admin foundation or a verified production stock operation.
slides.caption: October 13 · Existing sample cockpit walkthrough.

slides.title: “About 20 UPCs … the 4 tier access?”
slides.lead: The data request was completed; the access question received a scoped, honest answer.
slides.body:
20 synthetic products

Unique checksum-valid UPCs, CSV parity, legacy lookup aliases and derived summary counts. No real inventory import.

Local versus hosted

The local catalog showed 379 units, six attention items and 60 units due within two days. The hosted snapshot remained the older five-product demo.

Four-tier status

Admin, Staff, Viewer and Supplier are intended roles. Role foundations existed, but complete role routing and application-wide access were not finished.

slides.title: “Approved to run R03 and R06”
slides.lead: The named approval enabled a concrete isolated test sequence.
slides.body:
• TargetA separate local Supabase project with synthetic accounts and data, pinned tooling and explicit localhost endpoints.
  • VerificationSQL assertions, real Auth/API behavior, denial cases, cross-organisation isolation, races, retries, inventory fingerprints and restart checks.
  • PreservationBaseline and tested-state dumps, migration hashes and raw results were retained. Existing product and Onyx data stayed outside the target.

slides.title: “approving both”
slides.lead: The approval covered the corrected restore retry and R05 local Chrome validation.
slides.body:
Restore correction

Use the existing schema-owner-capable account, preserve failed evidence and prove the clean baseline could be restored.

Actual application

Build and serve the production Flutter entry locally; use real sign-in and synthetic data rather than the separate preview.

Result by cutoff

Restore passed and five UI groups passed. The connected sequence remained open for its remaining acceptance checks.

slides.title: The important boundaries were exercised
slides.lead: Real runtime results added evidence beyond the local source tests.
slides.body:
19concurrency groups
23Auth / API groups
61production DTO decodes
  • AuthorizationAll six setup RPCs, disallowed identities, anonymous access, cross-org requests, revocation, expiry/tampering and direct-table denial.
  • ConsistencySave/activation races, exact retries, stale revisions, lock waits, immutable references and coherent active-version reads.
  • PreservationEight setup-table fingerprints and six inventory-table fingerprints survived backend restart; synthetic inventory was unchanged.

slides.title: A failure became a verified recovery path
slides.lead: The original failed restore was kept, then the authorized correction was proven.
slides.body:
1

Preserve

Baseline and tested-state dumps retained with SHA-256 hashes.

2

Diagnose

Limited postgres role could not restore schema ownership.

3

Approve

Explicit permission for the existing supabase_admin restore account.

4

Verify

Five original migrations, no users/orgs/setup table; then reapply and assert.

The successful retry did not require new grants or credentials. Recovery evidence applies to the disposable test database, not a hosted production disaster-recovery exercise.

slides.title: Five connected UI groups passed
slides.lead: The app began exercising its actual SDK, forms and persistence path.
slides.body:
• Real sign-inAn authenticated admin reached setup through the Flutter application and real Auth service.
  • Draft handlingSaved values persisted; reload and explicit cancel/discard behavior were checked against server responses.
  • Configuration editingUnits and product packs, location create/rename/deactivate, and preset duplicate/version/edit/deactivate passed.
Still open by October 17: UI activation, competing sessions, lost-response recovery, offline reconnection, identity denial/switching, lifecycle/idle locking and authenticated narrow layouts. Do not equate page inspection with completed acceptance.

slides.title: The interruptions were recorded, not hidden
slides.lead: The report separates repaired issues from work that remained unverified.
slides.body:
Tooling and runtime

Docker startup interruptions; unexpected wildcard ports corrected before tests; fixture and relative shader-output errors corrected in the harness/build invocation.

Verification integrity

Credit-related interruptions were distinguished from executed commands. Historical records were preserved and later corrections added explicitly.

Release boundaries

No new production deployment, publication, commit/push/merge or rollout. No physical-device, camera or full four-role completion claim.

slides.title: The next checkpoint is application acceptance
slides.lead: Finish the approved connected sequence before moving the chapter forward.
slides.body:
• Complete the remaining UI checksActivation and immutable history; two-admin conflict; retry and offline recovery; role/identity changes; restart, background and idle locking; narrow authenticated layouts.
  • Close out with evidenceCompare inventory, preserve synthetic-state backups, perform scoped cleanup, update plan/ledger/index and save a final engineering handoff.
  • Keep the larger roadmap boundedS2 receiving/identity/queue, S3 stock actions and S4 paired rounds remain later implementation slices. Delivery retains separate approval.

slides.title: Evidence, not a timesheet
slides.lead: The categories intentionally remain separate.
slides.body:
No invented effort

This report contains no fabricated daily hours or productivity totals. Reconstructed date placement is marked and limited to an established work interval.

No blended test total

74 local cases, 19 concurrency groups, 23 API groups, 61 decoded responses and five UI groups measure different things and are not summed.

Historical cutoff

Only work attributable to October 4–17 is counted. October 19 report preparation and later Docker recovery events are excluded from period results.
